entities.name: Muhammad ibn Shakir al-Kutubi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abū ʿAbdallāh Muḥammad ibn Shākir al-Dārānī al-Dimashqī al-Kutubī (1287–1363) was a Syrian merchant and historian who documented his journeys across the Indian Ocean trade network.

As a merchant, Muhammad ibn Shakir al-Kutubi played a crucial role in the Silk Road, facilitating the exchange of goods and ideas between China and the Mediterranean.

His historical significance lies in his detailed accounts of the Indian Ocean trade, which provide valuable insights into the cultural and economic dynamics of the medieval Middle East.

Muhammad ibn Shakir al-Kutubi's writings also highlight the importance of the city of Basra as a major center of trade and commerce during the 14th century.

In his works, Muhammad ibn Shakir al-Kutubi expresses his admiration for the city of Mombasa, which he visited on one of his journeys, praising its strategic location and bustling port.

Despite his significance, Muhammad ibn Shakir al-Kutubi remains a relatively unknown figure outside of academic circles, overshadowed by more prominent historical figures of the time.

As a historian, Muhammad ibn Shakir al-Kutubi's work serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Indian Ocean trade network, which continues to shape global commerce and cultural exchange to this day.
